title: Hybrid Onramp: POC scope - Hosted → Private pathways
next_steps: Redwood: run 2 model-size microbenchmarks on dedicated capacity and share raw logs (by 2027-04-12)
Customer: share 1-week production traffic sample and 3 canonical prompts (by 2027-04-09)
action_items: Elena Martinez: Send pilot pricing, hosted vs dedicated vs private decision matrix PDF (due 2027-04-09)
Ravi Patel: Prepare benchmark plan and test script; include KV/prefix cache scenarios (due 2027-04-11)
Dana Reyes: Provide VPC peering/networking constraints doc and infra contact (due 2027-04-09)
Priya Singh: List required compliance artifacts (SOC2, ISO, data residency) and any additional encryption/HSM needs (due 2027-04-10)
summary: Kickoff to scope a hybrid POC with objectives to validate throughput/latency at 10k reqs/day, assess cost per 1M tokens, and define an onramp path from Redwood Hosted → Dedicated → Private (if required). Main concerns: data residency, KMS/HSM integration, networking/VPC peering, and fallbacks for capacity. Agreed next steps: exchange telemetry sample, run microbenchmarks, and reconvene with results.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-06
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Elena (Redwood AE), Ravi (Redwood SE), Jules (CS), Marco (CTO - Northbridge), Dana (Platform), Priya (InfoSec), Tomás (ML Eng)

[00:00] Elena Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, and then we'll jump into the hybrid onramp goals.
[00:18] Marco Liu: Yep, Marco here. Thanks.
[00:22] Dana Reyes: Dana on from infra.
[00:26] Priya Singh: Priya, InfoSec.
[00:29] Tomás Ortega: Tomás, ML.
[00:33] Elena Martinez: Great. So the purpose today is to define success criteria for a proof of concept that starts on Redwood Hosted and explores Dedicated and Private as needed. We'll cover workloads, benchmarks, and a proposed timeline.
[00:48] Ravi Patel: I'll add, we want to be explicit on what "success" means — latency p50/p95 targets, cost per 1M tokens, and operational runbooks so your ops team knows the cutover path.
[01:05] Marco Liu: High level: we have a deployed inference feature for parts recommendation. Traffic today is small but will spike. We estimate 10k requests/day during pilot with 30% peak traffic windows. Target latencies under 300ms p95 for small prompts; heavier prompts can be up to 800ms but we want tail behavior tight.
[01:29] Tomás Ortega: Just to add, model is a 7B-ish open model with quantized weights; we plan to use context up to 1k tokens. KV cache usage probably high because we do multi-turn sessions.
[01:45] Dana Reyes: Network-wise we can't expose PII to public endpoints except for synthetic data. So VPC peering for private deployment or dedicated with private networking is preferred.
[01:58] Priya Singh: From security: SOC2 is baseline, we also need KMS integration for customer-managed keys if we go private, and audit logs retention for 12 months. Data residency: EU only for pilot subset.
[02:17] Elena Martinez: Noted. Quick question — are you comfortable starting on Hosted with synthetic payloads to get early metrics? Or do you need everything in-VPC from day one?
[02:28] Marco Liu: We'd prefer to start hosted for speed but only with non-PII. If early metrics look good we'll move to Dedicated within the same week or two. The gating factor is Priya's checklist.
[02:40] Priya Singh: Correct. Hosted is OK for synthetic, but all real traffic must be on private or dedicated with VPC peering and KMS.
[02:48] Ravi Patel: Okay, so hybrid path: Hosted (fast iteration) → Dedicated (reserved capacity + VPC peering) → Private (if regulatory or on-prem constraints require it). We'll sketch the timeline and what we measure at each phase.
[03:05] Elena Martinez: Success criteria suggestion: 1) Latency p95 ≤ 350ms for shortest prompts, 2) Cost per 1M tokens below your target (TBD in pricing discussion), 3) No functional regressions on 200 canonical prompts, 4) Ability to run daily benchmarks and produce telemetry. Thoughts?
[03:26] Marco Liu: Those sound reasonable. For cost threshold we aim for a 40% reduction versus our current hosted vendor for similar quality.
[03:34] Tomás Ortega: On the regression tests — Tomás will own the prompt set; we want automatic reruns when we change model variants.
[03:42] Tomás Ortega: (inaudible) — and include sessions where KV cache warms up, that affects tail.
[03:49] Ravi Patel: Good catch. We'll include cold and warm cache scenarios, continuous batching at different QPS levels, and token-level cost measurement.
[03:58] Elena Martinez: Okay let's talk throughput and burn rate. You mentioned 10k reqs/day; what's the typical tokens per request?
[04:06] Tomás Ortega: Average 320 tokens in, 180 tokens out; call it ~500 tokens per request. Peak concurrency maybe 30 rps for a short window.
[04:18] Dana Reyes: For Dedicated sizing we want headroom — e.g., plan for 2x peak. We also prefer preemptible/spot for non-critical but need fallbacks.
[04:29] Ravi Patel: For a 7B quantized model, on Gpu X we'd expect around 12-18ms per token depending on kernel selection; but whole-request latency depends on batch formation and KV cache. We'll put numbers in the benchmark plan.
[04:44] Marco Liu: How do fallbacks work — if Dedicated is saturated does Redwood auto-fallback to Hosted? That's a risk for us if data crosses environments.
[04:53] Elena Martinez: Good question. We can configure routing policies. Default is prefer Dedicated, and if capacity is constrained and rules allow, route to Hosted with redaction and tokenization policies. But Priya, you'd need to approve data flows for that.
[05:06] Priya Singh: We need explicit write-up. No raw PII to Hosted under any fallback, only anonymized tokens. Also require audit trail showing data movement.
[05:17] Ravi Patel: We'll include a fail-open/closed policy matrix in the runbook.
[05:22] Elena Martinez: On benchmarks — we propose three microbenchmarks: 1) Latency suite (p50/p95/p99) single-request; 2) Throughput burst test (simulate 30 rps sustained for 5 minutes); 3) Mixed workload with KV cache and multi-turns to observe tail. We'll run these on Hosted and also on a Dedicated node configured to your desired instance type.
[05:43] Marco Liu: Sounds good. What about cost modeling? We need an estimate for per-hour Dedicated cost and per-token Hosted cost for the pilot.
[05:51] Elena Martinez: We'll provide a pricing comparison. Note Dedicated has a monthly reservation; we'll model the pilot as a 30-day reserved capacity with burst buffer. Hosted will be per-token. We'll show break-even points.
[06:05] Dana Reyes: Networking detail — for Dedicated we need VPC peering. For Private we need an on-prem appliance or air-gapped package; how long does Private usually take to provision?
[06:16] Ravi Patel: Private timelines vary — typically 6–10 weeks for on-prem depending on access, firewall rules, and KMS/HSM integration. Dedicated can be provisioned in 48–72 hours in many regions. Hosted: immediate.
[06:30] Marco Liu: That's longer than we hoped for Private. So hybrid path is sensible: get early data on Hosted, then Dedicated; only go Private if compliance forces it.
[06:41] Priya Singh: We'll evaluate Private only if certification or data residency demands it. Otherwise Dedicated with CMK (customer-managed key) is our preference.
[06:51] Elena Martinez: Great. Timeline proposal: Week 0 (this week) exchange telemetry and prompts; Week 1 run Hosted microbenchmarks on synthetic traffic; Week 2 run Dedicated microbenchmarks (we'll spin a reserved node) and compare; Week 3 start pilot traffic with non-PII; Week 4 expand to partial real traffic if InfoSec greenlights. Does that align?
[07:13] Marco Liu: Yes. We can be ready to provide telemetry by Friday.
[07:19] Tomás Ortega: Quick technical note — we'll need the bench harness. Do you have a recommended tool?
[07:25] Ravi Patel: We'll share a JMeter-based harness and a lightweight Python script that hits the SDK. Also a docker-compose for local validation. We'll version the scripts in a repo.
[07:36] Dana Reyes: For Dedicated we need network diagrams and public IP ranges to allow.
[07:40] Elena Martinez: We'll share the network diagram and the egress ranges.
[07:44] Priya Singh: Also a data flow diagram showing where PII may touch systems.
[07:49] Elena Martinez: We'll include that.
[07:52] Jules Kwan: I'll document the POC runbook and share after the call.
[07:56] Marco Liu: Any regulatory red flags? We operate in EU and US; some accounts require EU-only.
[08:02] Priya Singh: For EU-only, Dedicated in an EU-region with KMS in EU meets most needs. For on-prem you'd have to host the private stack in EU datacenter.
[08:14] Ravi Patel: On observability — Redwood Console exposes per-route latency and token-level cost, and we can open a read-only dashboard for your ops.
[08:22] Tomás Ortega: Can we get access to a sandbox console?
[08:25] Elena Martinez: Yes, we'll provision a sandbox org.
[08:29] Marco Liu: About model variants — we might test a 7B quantized and a 13B quantized to see quality vs cost tradeoffs. How long to swap model versions?
[08:37] Ravi Patel: In-hosting it's immediate within minutes; in Dedicated there's a deploy time depending on image warmup but typically under an hour for model swap if the artifact is pre-pulled. We'll note that.
[08:48] Priya Singh: Also need to know KV cache isolation per customer — is it siloed?
[08:52] Ravi Patel: Yes, each tenant has isolated KV caches and memory boundaries in Dedicated and Private. Hosted uses logical isolation; we'll provide the security whitepaper excerpt.
[09:02] Elena Martinez: Okay, let's capture the measurable success metrics we agreed:
[09:06] - Latency targets: p95 ≤ 350ms for small prompts; p99 < 900ms for heavy prompts
[09:12] - Throughput: sustain 30 rps for 5 minutes without p95 spikes > 2x baseline
[09:18] - Cost: target 40% improvement vs current vendor or explicit break-even on reserved capacity
[09:24] - Quality: no regressions on 200 canonical prompts (automated)
[09:30] - Security: KMS integration and VPC peering validated for real traffic
[09:36] Marco Liu: Good. Anything else?
[09:38] Tomás Ortega: Include failure injection tests — what happens to sessions if a node fails?
[09:42] Ravi Patel: We'll run a fault-injection scenario in the Dedicated run and document session continuity and fallback behavior.
[09:49] Elena Martinez: For benchmarks we'll need: canonical prompts, a traffic sample, and target instance types.
[09:55] Dana Reyes: I'll share the network contacts and a traffic sample by Friday.
[09:59] Marco Liu: We'll also want a one-page summary for execs showing cost/latency tradeoffs and recommended path.
[10:05] Elena Martinez: We'll produce an executive summary after the Dedicated run.
[10:09] Priya Singh: One more thing — encryption at rest: we need to confirm CMEK/HSM options and rotate keys every 90 days.
[10:17] Ravi Patel: We support CMEK and can integrate with HSM providers; rotation policies can be automated or manual. We'll include options.
[10:27] Elena Martinez: Alright, recap of next steps — we'll email the POC runbook, bench scripts, and pricing. You'll provide telemetry, prompts, and security checklist. We'll reconvene next Tuesday with initial Hosted benchmark results.
[10:44] Marco Liu: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[10:47] Dana Reyes: Thanks.
[10:49] Priya Singh: Thanks, bye.
[10:51] Elena Martinez: End meeting.

Notes on transcription: occasional words garbled (e.g., "kayvee cache" instead of KV cache), some speaker overlaps and short crosstalk.
